response.reason: The cited clause, Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011 Art. 26(3), specifically sets out the requirement that if the country of origin or place of provenance of a food is given and it is not the same as that of its primary ingredient, the origin of the primary ingredient must also be given or indicated as different. The verdict turns on this exact requirement, assessing whether both origins are declared and whether the requirement is satisfied. Therefore, the clause supports the verdict.
